correctness.rationale: The correct local Taylor coefficients give M_±(h)=E(h)±h²[A,B]/2+O(h³) in every finite-dimensional norm. An exact noncommutative subset expansion about E=e^{h(A+B)} bounds all ≥2 perturbation terms by O(n²h⁴ exp(O(nh²)))=O(h²) uniformly in signs and higher-order single-step terms by n O(h³)=O(h²). Hence the exact product error equals (h²/2)Σ ε_j E^{n-j}[A,B]E^{j-1}+O(h²) uniformly. Dividing by h^(3/2), the remainder vanishes and the coefficient array is bounded O(sqrt(h)); its independent centered signs satisfy the Cramér–Wold/Lindeberg CLT with covariance (1/4)∫vec(e^{(T-s)C}Ke^{sC})vec(...)^T ds, including singular support. Orthogonality gives the exact leading Frobenius second moment; an O(h²) L² remainder contributes o(h³). Invertible matrix exponentials show positivity iff K≠0; commuting generators yield exact equality for every path. Sign symmetry and local cancellation also give O(h²) mean difference. For oscillator A=[[0,1],[0,0]], B=[[0,0],[-1,0]], C is skew and K=diag(-1,1), so G(s) has squared Frobenius norm 2 for all s and T=1 gives exactly 1/2. Independently recomputed covariance by a 4-vector/16-second-moment transfer rather than executing submitted check.py, including a nonnormal matrix pair: oscillator normalized risks n=8,16,32,64 were 0.5072623814,0.5035147300,0.5017415971,0.5008687525, while the integral is 0.5; for a nonnormal pair the integral trace was 9.11305153335 and direct exact second-moment transfer converged toward it. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove the all-n statement.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: Zhang Algorithm 2 and Childs–Ostrander–Su §2 precede the fair forward/reverse Lie algorithm, its local commutator cancellation on averaging, and its mean-order benefit. Berger proves general near-identity random-matrix product CLTs, including stochastic Lie–Trotter formulas, and closely related 2026 published results give h^(3/2) commutator Gaussian covariance for *paired implicit Euler*, with deterministic O(h) bias and restricted positive-semidefinite matrices. The inspected statements do not imply the asserted full random-matrix Gaussian defect and exact Frobenius risk for independent explicit exponential forward/reverse products at h^(3/2) scale: this requires the separate centered-error expansion around e^{T(A+B)}. No exact dominating coverage identified, but general stochastic product CLTs may imply it under an as-yet-unworked reduction; priority is not certified.
residual_risks: Berger (1984) or another general stochastic product-array central limit theorem may subsume the result after an augmented-state or second-order expansion not explicitly resolved in this review.

The 2026 implicit pairing theorem uses essentially the same Gaussian commutator mechanism; assessing mathematical novelty of this exact exponential specialization is closer than its different integrator title suggests.

A specialist pre-2026 randomized geometric integrator or probabilistic numerical analysis treatment may already prove the exact trajectory-level formula; searchable abstracts alone cannot exclude this.
The exact h^(3/2) coefficient in the oscillator example is not a standalone originality claim.

value.rationale: The fundamental numerical-analysis question is whether a randomized first-order splitting whose ensemble mean has second-order accuracy is second-order for a single realization; the result proves no, generically its RMS defect is sharp h^(3/2). The matrix-wide nonzero-if-and-only-if commutator criterion, explicit propagated covariance and exact Frobenius risk coefficient quantify the distinction for arbitrary finite-dimensional real matrices without stability assumptions; the harmonic oscillator supplies a natural concrete benchmark. The fact is not merely a small numerical improvement or a renamed finite example, while the old random-order algorithm and basic CLT/commutator techniques are explicitly credited as prior. No optimality among randomized schemes or extension to infinite-dimensional problems follows.

final_claim: For arbitrary fixed real square matrices A,B, fixed T>0 and independent fair order choices at each step h=T/n, the product of exact forward/reversed Lie exponentials has h^(-3/2) matrix error converging in distribution to (1/2)∫_0^T e^{(T-s)(A+B)}[A,B]e^{s(A+B)} dW_s. Its vectorized covariance is the corresponding quarter integral of outer products and its scaled mean squared Frobenius error converges to the quarter integral of squared propagated commutator norms, strictly positive iff [A,B]≠0. E(P_n)-e^{T(A+B)}=O(h²), and the indicated oscillator pair has sharp risk 1/2 for T=1.
limitations: Only fixed finite-dimensional real matrices, fair independent signs, fixed T and exact exponentials.
The Gaussian matrix law may be singular; no componentwise independence claim.
Neither dimension-uniform nor unbounded-operator, nonlinear-flow, long-time or finite-step distributional rate result is proved.
The independent check is numerical finite-grid corroboration, not an exhaustive all-dimensional proof.
Best-of-knowledge literature limitations and close predecessor implicit Gaussian commutator results are retained in originality residual_risks.
